correctness.rationale: Reconstructed actual frozen RESULT.md (all definitions, length/letter quantifiers, positive-law necessity, and L=1/n<L boundary). For a cross-bifix-free equal-length code, starts closer than L cannot co-occur, whereas starts at least L apart use disjoint independent coordinate blocks; expanding E ∏(1+(z−1)I_i) gives exactly the weighted independence polynomial of the (L−1)-power of a path with weights a_i=P(I_i=1). Neighbor sets split into left/right cliques, hence this graph is claw-free. The published Chudnovsky–Seymour theorem (checked through Bencs Theorem 1.8 complete proof) applies to the nonnegative weighted case through rational clique blow-ups and coefficient limits, and all roots of normalized nonnegative PGF are ≤0, forcing a Bernoulli-product factorization. For a bordered word with shortest period s, at n=L+s the unique possible overlap is starts 1 and s+1, no triple is possible; E N=(s+1)π and P(N=2)=π²/h. A quadratic PGF is PB iff real rooted; direct discriminant Δ=π²((s+1)²−4/h), giving h≥4/(s+1)². Making one shared-prefix letter rare while retaining strictly positive other letter probabilities forces h→0, proving converse. For iid code probability a, k legal start placements are exactly binomial(n−(L−1)k,k), giving stated full PGF. Independently enumerated all 3^8 ternary words for a nonstationary cross-bifix-free 2-code, exact rational agreement; earliest-overlap direct enumeration for four overlapping binary motifs at three positive iid biases each; iid n=11 stationary full four-mass distribution. These finite tests corroborate but do not prove the arbitrary-n theorem.
residual_risks: Claw-free real-rootedness is a substantial externally proved graph theorem, not an independently reconstructed proof of its most general version; read Bencs's complete alternate proof.
Finite-rational enumerations do not prove arbitrary word length, alphabet or nonidentical laws; generality rests on indicator expansion plus published theorem.
PB Bernoulli probabilities exist by real-rooted PGF factorization, not algorithmically supplied for arbitrary nonstationary marginals.
First-overlap threshold is not claimed to classify every larger sample size.

value.rationale: The word border is a natural combinatorial obstruction to nonoverlapping occurrences, and Poisson–binomial representability is a meaningful exact structural property of dependent local-pattern counts. The theorem gives a complete infinite-family iff classification over all n and all independent, potentially non-identical source marginals, a strictly positive-iid necessary counterlaw for every self-overlapping word, and a sharp first-overlap parameter threshold. Cross-bifix-free code sufficiency expands the class of natural word patterns to nonstationary sources. Stationary placement enumeration is related to known avoidance formulas, so the primary value is the distributional real-rootedness/if-and-only-if bridge and sharp converse, not counting a known table again. This supplies exact input for pattern probability, Bernoulli-sum concentration/shape results and diagnostics; it is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a routine renaming of an already stated word-count theorem.
residual_risks: A future bibliography might establish this special connection already in classical renewal/word-cluster literature; under that discovery V and O must be reconsidered for the surviving novelty.
The finite sample first-overlap criterion is local to n=L+s; longer-length PB status for a given biased bordered word is not classified.
The stationary formula is straightforward from previously known nonoverlapping-code enumeration and not an independent major contribution.

final_claim: For any finite alphabet with at least two letters and a fixed length-L consecutive literal word w, its count in every n≥L independent (not necessarily identically distributed) letter source is a Poisson–binomial sum iff w is unbordered (equivalently, iff PB holds for every n and every strictly positive iid alphabet law). Equal-length cross-bifix-free code counts inherit PB for independent nonstationary sources, while for a bordered word with minimum positive period s the first-overlap n=L+s count is PB exactly when prefix mass h=Pr(w_1...w_(L-s))≥4/(s+1)^2. In iid cross-bifix-free case pgf is Σ_{k≤floor(n/L)} C(n−(L−1)k,k)a^k(z−1)^k.
